title: Leaf count after pruning a subprotocol
statement: Let $X$, $Y$, and $\alpha$ be types, and let $s$ and $p$ be deterministic two-party communication protocols with inputs in $X$ and $Y$ and outputs in $\alpha$. Suppose $s$ is a rooted subtree of $p$ and has strictly fewer leaves than $p$. Then pruning $s$ from $p$ yields a protocol with exactly $L(p)-L(s)$ leaves, where $L(q)$ denotes the number of leaves of protocol $q$.
hypotheses_covered: $s$ and $p$ are protocols with input types $X,Y$ and output type $\alpha$
replaced:
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol and let $s$ be a subprotocol
of $p$, that is, a rooted subtree of $p$. Write $L(q)$ for the number of leaves (output
nodes) of a protocol $q$, and suppose that $L(s) < L(p)$. Then the protocol obtained by
pruning $s$ out of $p$ has exactly $L(p) - L(s)$ leaves.
